title: Anthropic Nears Deal With Trump Administration to Restore Access to Fable AI Model
summary: Anthropic reached a deal with the Trump administration to restore public access to its Fable AI model after roughly two and a half weeks of restricted access tied to cybersecurity concerns. The episode has renewed debate over how the U.S. government balances export and access controls on frontier AI models against industry and national-security interests.

title: SpaceX Showed Investors Prototype of Elon Musk's New AI Device
summary: SpaceX presented investors with a prototype of a sleek, handset-like AI device designed to integrate technology from xAI, Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company. The demonstration signals SpaceX's growing involvement in consumer AI hardware alongside its core space and satellite businesses.

title: The World's Top Economists Are Sounding the Alarm on AI
summary: A growing number of prominent economists have joined warnings about the potential global economic fallout if the current AI investment boom turns into a bust. Their concerns center on how concentrated AI-related capital spending and valuations have become across the economy.

title: Cyber Insurers Want to See Policyholders Take AI Seriously
summary: Cyber insurers are increasingly requiring policyholders to demonstrate concrete safeguards against AI-related security risks before offering or renewing coverage. Insurers are scrutinizing exposure to compromised AI tools, patching speed, and vendor vetting as AI-driven threats become a material underwriting factor.

title: House Lawmakers Grill NTIA Chief Over BEAD Broadband Deployment Delays
summary: At a June 30 House Energy and Commerce subcommittee hearing, NTIA Administrator Arielle Roth faced bipartisan criticism over the slow rollout of the $42.5 billion Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment (BEAD) program, with lawmakers noting only Nebraska and Louisiana have connected any locations so far. Legislators also raised concerns about delayed non-deployment fund guidance and provider dropouts, including Resound Networks declining more than $100 million in BEAD awards.

title: Verizon and BT Form $4 Billion Joint Venture for Global Enterprise Customers
summary: Verizon and BT Group agreed to merge their international enterprise operations into a 50:50 joint venture worth roughly $4 billion in combined annual revenue, serving more than 3,000 multinational customers across over 180 countries. Verizon will make a $625 million equalization payment to BT as part of the deal, which still requires regulatory approval.

title: EchoStar's Dish DBS and Wireless Units File for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy
summary: EchoStar's Dish DBS satellite-TV subsidiary and certain wireless units filed for prepackaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy on June 30 after being unable to repay $2 billion in senior secured notes due July 1, a shortfall linked to delays in closing a previously announced $23 billion spectrum sale to AT&T. The filing is also intended to facilitate the wind-down of the legacy Dish Wireless 5G network, backed by a $2.4 billion FCC escrow fund and supported by holders of more than 88% of Dish's debt.

title: MIT-Microsoft Study Ranks 101 Enterprise Tasks by Agent Confidence
summary: A study by MIT in partnership with Microsoft surveyed 300 global technology experts to rank 101 enterprise tasks across AI, data, and cloud workflows by how confident they are in AI agents completing them independently. Confidence was highest for generating reports and boilerplate code but dropped sharply for complex, multi-step reasoning tasks, with 59% of respondents saying human oversight remains critical for higher-stakes work.

title: Goldman Sachs: AI Driving an Industrial "Supercycle" Across the Real Economy
summary: Goldman Sachs published a report arguing that AI is accelerating industrial transformation across both digital and physical sectors faster, more broadly, and more capital-intensively than prior technology cycles. The bank frames this as an investment supercycle spanning infrastructure, energy, and industrial applications of AI.

title: Deloitte: Most Enterprises Say Their AI Operating Model Must Change Within 18 Months
summary: Deloitte surveyed more than 660 technology executives worldwide and found 81% believe they can already deploy and govern AI at scale, yet nearly 75% expect their operating model will need to change within 12 to 18 months to sustain progress. The findings suggest governance structures, not the underlying technology, are the near-term bottleneck for enterprise AI adoption.

title: Zain Wins 25-Year Syria Telecoms Licence for $750M
summary: Zain Group secured a 25-year telecommunications licence in Syria worth $750 million following a competitive tender process. The award is intended to support modernization of the country's existing telecom infrastructure.

title: UK's CMA Fast-Tracks In-Depth Probe into £2B Fibre Deal
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority launched an in-depth investigation into Nexfibre's proposed £2 billion takeover of rival broadband provider Netomnia. The probe introduces regulatory uncertainty for further consolidation in the UK fibre broadband market.

title: Circle's New Rival
summary: Stripe, Visa, Mastercard, Coinbase, BlackRock, and BNY are leading a consortium of more than 140 firms to launch a new stablecoin called Open USD later this year, aiming to challenge Circle and Tether's dominance of the roughly $300 billion stablecoin market. The venture plans to share reserve income with distribution partners and forgo conversion fees; Circle shares fell 18% on the news, though past multi-partner stablecoin efforts such as Facebook's Libra and Paxos's USDG have struggled to gain scale.

title: OpenAI Selects Law Firms Cooley, Wachtell to Prepare for IPO as Anthropic Files Confidentially
summary: OpenAI and Anthropic's rivalry is reportedly extending into a race toward public markets: Anthropic has made a confidential IPO filing, while OpenAI has retained law firms Cooley and Wachtell to help prepare for its own potential listing. Other reporting from The Information indicates some investors remain skeptical of both companies' IPO prospects, and that OpenAI and Anthropic employees have already cashed out roughly $14 billion combined through secondary share sales.

title: Nvidia Funds Security Firm Verkada at $5.8 Billion Valuation
summary: Nvidia is investing an unspecified amount in Verkada, a maker of security cameras and related software, at a $5.8 billion valuation matching the company's December financing round led by Alphabet's CapitalG. With technical assistance from Nvidia engineers, Verkada said the precision of its video AI has improved.

title: Ayar Labs Joins AI Chip Funding Spree
summary: Ayar Labs, an 11-year-old optical networking startup, is in talks to raise at least $200 million at a valuation sharply above the $3.75 billion it fetched in its prior round. The deal reflects a broader surge of investor interest in startups making optical, light-based components to replace copper wiring for faster connections between AI chips, a category that also includes competitors Lightmatter and Celestial AI.

title: Bending Spoons Stock Jumps 40% in Trading Debut
summary: Bending Spoons, the Italian company known for acquiring and overhauling struggling digital brands such as AOL, Evernote and Vimeo, saw its shares jump 40% on their first day of trading as a public company. That compared with a more modest 4% first-day gain for scooter rental firm Lime, which also debuted the same week following SpaceX's high-profile public offering.

title: The Anthropic Fable Ban Is Over. The Battle Over How to Tame AI Has Just Begun.
summary: Washington has lifted its block on Anthropic's Fable AI model, but the reversal has intensified debate over how the U.S. should regulate increasingly capable AI systems. WSJ reporting notes that reasoning models and AI agents are evolving faster than regulators can track, making AI a much harder target to govern than industries like autos or air travel. A new Trump administration security-approval process now effectively determines when a frontier model is considered safe enough for release.

title: Read the Emails Revealing How Anthropic's Pentagon Relationship Fell Apart
summary: Internal emails reviewed by the Wall Street Journal show Pentagon undersecretary Emil Michael and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei exchanged messages for months over AI safety guardrails before the relationship deteriorated. The correspondence illustrates growing friction between Anthropic and the Defense Department over how the company's models can be used in national-security contexts.

title: U.S. Adds 57,000 Jobs in June, Missing Forecasts as Unemployment Rate Falls to 4.2%
summary: The U.S. economy added 57,000 jobs in June, falling short of economists' expectations, the Labor Department reported. The unemployment rate nonetheless ticked down to 4.2%, better than the 4.3% rate economists had forecast.

title: Tesla Caps Employee AI Spend at $200 per Week After Adoption Push
summary: Tesla has capped how much individual employees can spend on AI tools at $200 per week, following a companywide push to expand AI adoption among staff. The cap reflects growing corporate scrutiny of AI tool costs as usage scales across large workforces.

title: Palantir CEO: Some U.S. Government Customers Switched to Open Source AI
summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp said some U.S. government customers have shifted toward open-source AI models rather than working directly with OpenAI or Anthropic. Following a combative CNBC appearance in which he accused the two AI labs of overcharging customers and misusing their data, Karp positioned Palantir as a trusted intermediary between government agencies and AI vendors.

title: Microsoft Memo Details AI App Overhaul to 'Earn the Right to Exist'
summary: An internal Microsoft memo reportedly says the company plans to consolidate and overhaul its various Copilot chatbot products, with executives telling teams their AI apps must 'earn the right to exist.' The memo points to a broader push at Microsoft to sharpen its consumer and enterprise AI product strategy amid intensifying competition.

title: AI Data Centers Are Becoming Wall Street's Next Trade
summary: The Information reports that AI data centers have shifted from being primarily a technology infrastructure story to a financial one, as investors increasingly treat the compute capacity, power contracts and financing structures behind frontier AI models as tradeable assets. The shift reflects the scale of capital now required to build and finance the infrastructure that AI model developers depend on.

title: Anthropic in Talks With Samsung to Manufacture Custom AI Chip
summary: Anthropic has begun early-stage work on designing its own AI chip and has held talks with Samsung about manufacturing it, The Information reports. The move would follow other AI labs' efforts to reduce dependence on Nvidia by developing custom silicon for training and running their models.

title: Why Microsoft's Real Value Is Close to $3.8 Trillion, or $500 a Share
summary: The Information estimates Microsoft's sum-of-the-parts value is closer to $3.8 trillion, or roughly $500 per share, when its major businesses are valued individually rather than as a single combined entity. The analysis suggests certain segments of Microsoft's business may be undervalued relative to comparable standalone companies.

title: Nvidia Will Backstop Customers' GPUs, Take a Cut of Their Cloud Revenues
summary: Nvidia is using its balance sheet to help more companies afford its expensive AI chips, agreeing to financially backstop young cloud providers that rent out its GPUs in exchange for a cut of those providers' cloud revenue. The arrangement is designed to support demand for Nvidia's chips while creating a new recurring revenue stream tied to how customers actually use them.

title: Zero Point Cryogenics Wants to Freeze the Quantum World
summary: Edmonton-based Zero Point Cryogenics is building near-absolute-zero cryogenic freezers needed to operate quantum computers, positioning the company as a supplier to the growing quantum computing industry. The report highlights a small but expanding cluster of Canadian quantum hardware firms serving global quantum computing developers.

title: AI Data Centers Use Far More Water Than Most Tech Giants Report
summary: AI data centers consume substantially more water than most tech companies publicly disclose, largely because indirect water use at the power plants supplying their electricity is typically excluded from corporate reporting; only Meta currently discloses this indirect figure. A 2024 Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory analysis found indirect water consumption for U.S. data centers has historically run about 12 times greater than their direct on-site use. Separately, climate consulting firm Carbon Direct estimates $170 billion of planned AI data-center capacity has been blocked, stalled, or canceled since 2024.

title: Microsoft Commits $2.5 Billion to New Applied AI Consulting Effort
summary: Microsoft commercial CEO Judson Althoff announced a new business unit, Microsoft Frontier Company, dedicated to helping large customers deploy and customize AI applications. The company is committing $2.5 billion and assigning 6,000 employees to the effort, which will be led by sales president Rodrigo Kede Lima. The move follows similar "forward deployed engineer" initiatives from Amazon, Google, Palantir, Meta, and OpenAI aimed at helping enterprise customers get better returns from AI spending.

title: Google Loses Fight Against Record €4.1 Billion Android Antitrust Fine
summary: The European Court of Justice dismissed Google's final appeal against a €4.1 billion ($4.7 billion) fine over its Android operating system, ending an eight-year antitrust battle that began with a 2018 European Commission ruling. Regulators found Google had required phone makers to pre-install Google Search and Chrome to access the Play Store and tied ad revenue sharing to exclusivity against rival search engines. The case is one of three antitrust actions in which the EU has fined Google more than $9 billion combined since 2017.

title: Alibaba Bans Employees From Using Claude
summary: Alibaba Group has barred employees from using Anthropic's Claude Code and ordered the removal of Claude models from company computers, citing security concerns following a controversy over hidden code that could detect whether users were in China. The ban follows Anthropic's recent accusation that Alibaba illicitly used Claude models to train its own AI systems through distillation. Alibaba has separately sued the U.S. Department of Defense over its inclusion on a Pentagon blacklist of Chinese companies with alleged military ties.

title: SoftBank Plans to Rent AI Computing Capacity to U.S. Companies
summary: SoftBank Group and its telecom unit SoftBank Corp announced plans to rent AI computing capacity to U.S. companies starting in April, through a new neocloud venture called SB Neo Inc. The venture aims to scale to 10 gigawatts of capacity to meet AI data center demand, putting SoftBank in direct competition with cloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius Group. SoftBank is borrowing heavily to invest across the AI supply chain, including chips, servers, data centers, and power.

title: Kuaishou Announces Kling AI Video Unit's Fundraising at $15 Billion Valuation
summary: Kuaishou Technology said its Kling AI video unit has agreed to raise nearly $3 billion at a $15 billion pre-money valuation, with Kuaishou retaining a 68.33% stake after the round closes. The funding, led by Chinese investment firms CPE and Guofang Investment along with Tencent and Abu Dhabi-based BlueFive, values Kling below the $20 billion target Kuaishou had sought earlier this year. Kling's first-quarter revenue reportedly surged 300% year-over-year to an annualized run rate of about $500 million in March.

title: Nvidia's Longtime Sales Chief Retires
summary: Jay Puri, Nvidia's top sales executive and a direct report to CEO Jensen Huang, stepped down from his day-to-day role after 21 years at the company; Microsoft sales executive Nicholas Parker was named as his successor, starting August 24. Puri, 71, is expected to remain as a senior adviser and is credited with helping transition Nvidia from a consumer gaming brand into an enterprise AI chip supplier.

title: OpenAI Has Discussed Size of Stake U.S. Government Could Take
summary: OpenAI has held preliminary discussions with the U.S. government about the size of an equity stake it might take in the company, with the Financial Times earlier reporting a proposed 5% stake from OpenAI's CEO. The proposal follows an OpenAI white paper floating a public wealth fund seeded by AI company assets, an idea similar to a bill from Senator Bernie Sanders proposing a 50% government stake in top AI firms. Anthropic has made a similar public fund proposal but has not discussed a government stake directly with the administration.

title: Tesla Vehicle Sales Rebounded 25% in Second Quarter
summary: Tesla's global vehicle deliveries rose 25% year-over-year to 480,000 in the second quarter, with 468,000 of those being Model 3 or Model Y vehicles, following a sales slump in 2025. The company's energy storage business deployed 13.5 gigawatt-hours of batteries in the quarter, up 41% year-over-year, while Tesla shares fell 7% on the day of the announcement. Rising European gas prices tied to the Iran war have been credited with boosting electric vehicle demand broadly, including for Tesla and Chinese rivals such as BYD.

title: Nvidia to Financially Backstop Younger Neocloud Firms Amid Funding Boom
summary: Nvidia is offering to financially backstop smaller "neocloud" firms that rent out AI servers, in exchange for a share of their revenues, as competition intensifies among the growing number of companies entering the sector. The move comes as SoftBank launched a new U.S. neocloud venture and AI infrastructure startup Together AI raised $800 million, underscoring plentiful funding despite concerns about overbuilding. Analysts note Nvidia's backstopping could increase financial risk for smaller, less-established players relative to larger cloud providers like AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

title: Freshfields Wins Role in Anthropic's IPO
summary: British law firm Freshfields has been retained by Anthropic's bankers to work on the company's initial public offering, which is expected to raise tens of billions of dollars at a valuation exceeding $1 trillion. Freshfields, founded in 1743, opened its first Silicon Valley office in 2020 and has previously advised on deals including Google's $32 billion acquisition of Wiz and the European portion of SpaceX's $86 billion share offering. Rival law firms Cooley, Wachtell Lipton, and Latham & Watkins are advising OpenAI on its own competing IPO process.

title: Lime Goes Public at $1.6 Billion Valuation
summary: Scooter and bike rental company Lime went public on the Nasdaq this week at a $1.6 billion valuation, generating returns for early investors including Andreessen Horowitz, which held a 5% stake at the time of listing. Lime's prospectus had warned the company faced possible bankruptcy without a public listing. CEO Wayne Ting framed the IPO as a bet on an "AI-resilient" physical-world business, comparable in positioning to companies like Oura, Reformation, and Jersey Mike's.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Ottawa's Elusive AI Startup
summary: Turbopuffer, a three-year-old Ottawa startup with a small team, has become an infrastructure provider for major AI companies including Anthropic and is on pace to generate roughly $100 million in revenue. Co-founders Simon Eskildsen, a former Shopify engineer, and Justine Li built a lower-cost method for AI systems to search stored data, and have deliberately avoided marketing and media attention despite the company's rapid growth.

title: HCLTech Inks $1.1 Billion AI Deal With European Firm
summary: Indian IT services company HCLTech secured a $1.1 billion contract with a major European company to deploy AI services and help manage its enterprise technology offerings. The deal adds to a wave of large AI services contracts among global IT consultancies as enterprises look for help implementing AI at scale.

title: Meta CEO Downbeat on AI Gains So Far
summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg reportedly told employees that the company's AI agent strategy is progressing more slowly than expected and that its AI-driven reorganization earlier this year has yet to deliver anticipated gains. The comments add to a broader pattern of large enterprises, including Uber and Starbucks, expressing frustration over difficulty generating measurable returns from AI investment.

title: Amazon Leo Launches 29 More Satellites Ahead of Broadband Debut
summary: Amazon is on track to launch its Leo broadband service later this year after a United Launch Alliance rocket successfully deployed 29 more satellites, bringing the constellation's total to 396. The launch keeps Amazon on pace to compete with SpaceX's Starlink in the satellite broadband market.

title: Anthropic in Talks With Samsung to Manufacture Custom AI Chip
summary: Anthropic is reportedly in early-stage discussions with Samsung Electronics about serving as a manufacturing partner for a custom AI chip, according to people familiar with the matter. No agreement has been finalized, and the talks remain preliminary. A custom chip effort would align Anthropic with rivals such as OpenAI and Google, which have pursued their own dedicated silicon.

title: Apple to Debut Five New iPhones by 2027
summary: Apple reportedly plans to launch at least five new iPhone models between the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027, while also ramping up production of foldable devices. The expanded lineup suggests an acceleration in Apple's product cadence and a deeper push into new device categories.

title: The Quest to Make Humanoid Robots Safe Enough for Humans
summary: The Wall Street Journal examines the safety engineering challenges facing humanoid robot makers after several viral incidents of robots malfunctioning around people. Manufacturers report no serious injuries or deaths to date, but growing concern centers on the robots approaching 200 pounds in weight, raising the stakes if a bipedal machine loses power near a person. Companies are responding with layered safeguards, including emergency stop buttons and chip-level safety systems, such as a new Nvidia system built on its Blackwell chips that can interpret sensor data and halt a robot when conditions become unsafe.

title: OpenAI vs. Anthropic: AI's IPO Race Begins
summary: Anthropic has begun discussing a possible initial public offering as soon as the fourth quarter of 2026, shortly after raising funding at a valuation near $900 billion, while OpenAI is also moving toward a future listing. Reporting indicates OpenAI's CEO and CFO differ on how quickly to pursue an IPO, with the company projected to burn well over $100 billion in cash before turning a profit. The competing timelines could put Anthropic ahead of OpenAI in reaching public markets despite OpenAI's larger valuation and profile.

title: Kalshi Nears $2 Billion in Annualized Revenue Amid Informal IPO Talks
summary: Prediction-market operator Kalshi has surpassed $2 billion in annualized revenue, roughly three times its level in November, driven by a surge in betting volume tied to NBA and World Cup events. The company is reportedly holding informal discussions about a possible initial public offering. Kalshi's growth adds it to a widening list of companies, including OpenAI and SpaceX, weighing near-term public listings.

title: Walmart's Amazon-Sized Ads Opportunity
summary: Walmart has built an advertising business large enough that it now generates more ad revenue than smaller social platforms such as Snap or Pinterest, according to The Information. The growth follows Walmart's roughly $1.4 billion acquisition of ad-tech startup Vibe, intended to help it sell more advertising to marketers on streaming platforms. The expansion positions Walmart's media business as an increasingly significant competitor to Amazon's advertising unit.

title: BCG's CXO Guide to AI Token Cost Control
summary: Boston Consulting Group published guidance urging enterprise leaders to treat AI token spending as a governed cost center rather than an open-ended expense, introducing a "return on AI" metric to weigh value against spend. The report argues that decisions about AI models, architecture, and control infrastructure should be evaluated together rather than optimized solely for the lowest per-token price. BCG contends that companies achieving the best financial outcomes from AI will be those maximizing returns, not simply those spending the least or the most.

title: Palantir Publishes "AI Sovereignty" Manifesto, Criticizes Rivals' Token Pricing
summary: Palantir published a nine-point manifesto describing what it calls "AI sovereignty," urging organizations to keep their data in-house, control their own model weights, and avoid token-based pricing for AI services. The manifesto criticizes what Palantir calls "tokenmaxxing" and implicitly challenges the business models of OpenAI and Anthropic. Palantir CEO Alex Karp separately called competitors' token-based pricing "insane" in a television interview shortly before the post.

title: Big Tech Has Suddenly Flipped on the AI Jobs Wipeout Scenario
summary: Major technology companies have quietly softened earlier warnings that artificial intelligence would trigger sweeping job losses, as public opinion toward AI has grown more negative. Executives including OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei, who previously forecast substantial workforce disruption, are now emphasizing that AI will keep workers at the center of business operations. A survey cited in the report found the share of CEOs expecting AI to cause significant headcount reductions fell from about 46% in January 2025 to 20% in May 2026.

title: OpenAI's Biggest Backers Bet on Josh Kushner's AI Roll-Up Machine
summary: Some of OpenAI's largest investors are reportedly putting capital behind Thrive Holdings, an AI-focused roll-up vehicle led by Thrive Capital founder Josh Kushner that buys and operates traditional services businesses. OpenAI itself has taken an ownership stake in Thrive Holdings and agreed to embed its researchers with the vehicle's portfolio companies to build customized AI models. The arrangement deepens financial ties between OpenAI's investor base and its commercial applications beyond its core chatbot business.

title: Smith and Ford revive push for a west-to-east oil pipeline
summary: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith and Ontario Premier Doug Ford are reviving efforts to build a new oil pipeline running from the Alberta oilpatch to eastern Canada, according to The Logic. The push aims to reduce Canadian reliance on the U.S. market for oil exports and follows years of stalled interprovincial pipeline proposals. Jurisdictional disputes between federal and provincial governments have historically been the main obstacle to similar projects.

title: Apple's ambitious plans for 5 new iPhones by 2027
summary: Apple is reportedly planning to launch at least five new iPhone models between late 2026 and the first half of 2027, including its first foldable device, a standard iPhone 18, and a new iPhone Air model, according to a Nikkei Asia report cited by CNBC. The company has raised its foldable iPhone production target to roughly 10 million units, up from an earlier forecast of 7 to 8 million, with the foldable expected to be priced around $2,500. Apple has also explored Chinese chip suppliers to address AI-driven memory component shortages.

title: How Small Firms Use Claude to Quit Salesforce
summary: Small and mid-sized firms are increasingly replacing Salesforce and other traditional enterprise software with custom workflows built on Anthropic's Claude, according to The Information. The trend reflects broader unease inside Salesforce about AI assistants encroaching on core CRM functions. It points to a potential shift in how smaller businesses procure and build software as AI models take on tasks once handled by dedicated enterprise applications.

title: KT sets aside $12B to fuel AI platform ambition
summary: South Korean telecom operator KT unveiled a roughly $12 billion (KRW18 trillion) five-year investment plan to transform into what it calls an AI platform company under its new CEO. The spending is allocated across network infrastructure, IT and security, data centers, and submarine cable capacity. KT said the plan aims to build capabilities in AI, cybersecurity, and next-generation connectivity including 6G.

title: SKT targets 15GW data centre capacity
summary: SK Telecom outlined plans to build 15 gigawatts of AI-capable data center capacity in South Korea, starting with 5GW online from 2029 and an additional 10GW from 2035. The company is positioning itself as a regional AI infrastructure hub, with an initial site in Ulsan and planned clusters in the Gyeongsang and Jeolla regions, and cited McKinsey forecasts of 19-22% annual growth in data center demand. A single gigawatt-class AI data center is estimated to cost roughly KRW70 trillion, to be financed through company investment, partner capital, and project financing.

title: Tesla expands Robotaxi service to Miami
summary: Tesla expanded its Robotaxi service to a section of western and central Miami, making Florida the first state outside Texas to host the fully autonomous service. Unlike Tesla's earlier Austin deployment, which used in-vehicle safety supervisors, the Miami service launched without human supervision from day one. Tesla has said it plans further expansions to Orlando, Tampa, Phoenix, and Las Vegas.

title: Alibaba, Bytedance Halt Personalized AI Features as Regulations Tighten
summary: ByteDance and Alibaba are shutting down personalized AI companion features on their Doubao and Qwen platforms ahead of new Chinese rules on anthropomorphic AI that take effect July 15. The regulations, issued by China's Cyberspace Administration and other agencies, require anti-addiction safeguards and periodic break reminders that conflict with how persistent-memory AI companions are designed. Affected users have until mid-October to export their data before it is deleted.

title: Singapore Files New Charges in Nvidia Chip Fraud Case
summary: Singapore prosecutors filed additional charges against four individuals and four companies accused of misrepresenting the end-users of servers containing restricted Nvidia AI chips. Authorities allege the hardware was routed through Singapore before being shipped onward to Malaysia or China in an effort to evade U.S. export controls. The case is one of several recent enforcement actions targeting alleged circumvention of chip export restrictions in Southeast Asia.

title: Quebec Ink: Quebec's era of endless, cheap electricity is coming to an end
summary: A Quebec Ink column by Martin Patriquin argues that the province's decades-long era of abundant, low-cost electricity is ending as demand rises from data centers, electrification, and industrial growth. Quebec has long relied on inexpensive hydroelectric power as an economic advantage for households and industry. The column suggests the province will need to rebalance supply commitments and pricing as demand pressures mount.

title: Microsoft to Cut 4,800 Jobs, Mostly in Xbox and Sales
summary: Microsoft is laying off about 4,800 employees, roughly 2% of its workforce, primarily in its sales organization and Xbox gaming division. Xbox will cut 1,600 roles immediately and sell at least four game studios, with CEO Asha Sharma telling staff the unit "is not healthy" and operates at margins 3-10x lower than comparable businesses.

title: Broadcom and Apple Extend Tech Collaboration Through 2031
summary: Broadcom and Apple agreed to extend their custom-chip collaboration through 2031 under new multiyear agreements disclosed in a securities filing. The deal reinforces Broadcom's role as a key networking-chip partner for Apple's AI server hardware, and sent Broadcom shares up 4% in premarket trading.

title: AI Enters a New Stage of Financial Innovation as Debt Markets Swell
summary: Research firm SemiAnalysis projects that AI debt financing will grow into a multi-trillion-dollar credit market, with more than $7 trillion outstanding by 2029, rivaling the US mortgage-backed securities market. The report argues hyperscalers' balance sheets alone cannot backstop that scale of borrowing, so neoclouds and AI labs need to broaden their customer base beyond a handful of large cloud providers to sustain data-center financing.

title: AI Infrastructure Startup Nscale Secures $900 Million for Data-Center Buildout
summary: Nvidia-backed AI infrastructure startup Nscale secured a $900 million line of credit to expand data-center capacity across Europe, the US, and Asia-Pacific. The company, also backed by Dell and Nokia, had raised $2 billion earlier this year at a $14.6 billion valuation.

title: Samsung Forecasts Record Second-Quarter Operating Profit
summary: Samsung Electronics projected a record second-quarter operating profit of about $58.47 billion, roughly 19 times higher year-over-year, driven by surging demand for AI memory chips and strong server DRAM pricing. The forecast comes amid broader market jitters over whether AI infrastructure spending is sustainable.

title: Why SK Hynix Isn't as Cheap as It Looks
summary: SK Hynix, which is preparing to raise about $28 billion in a US listing this week, has become one of the world's most profitable companies, with analysts projecting nearly $150 billion in net income this year, up from losses three years ago. Despite its stock more than tripling in 2026, the shares trade at a forward P/E of around 7, reflecting investor wariness that the memory industry's historically cyclical downturns will eventually follow the current AI-driven upturn.

title: Nokia's New Act: Supplying the AI Data Center Boom
summary: Nokia shares have surged roughly 90% this year as the company pivots from its legacy handset business to become a major supplier of AI data-center infrastructure equipment.

title: Will Someone Finally Blink in the AI Spending War?
summary: A Wall Street Journal analysis asks whether major tech companies have overbuilt AI computing capacity, noting that if Meta begins renting out its excess compute to other businesses, it could be an early signal that AI infrastructure investment has outpaced actual demand.

title: AI Giants Are Handing Out Tons of Free Computing Power to Grab Startup Share
summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI model developers are offering startups discounted or free cloud computing power, tokens, and early access to new models as they compete to lock in future enterprise customers. The push comes as AI labs seek durable revenue streams large enough to justify their capital-spending commitments.

title: New Cyber Incident Reporting Rules Coming in September
summary: Four years after Congress passed the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency is expected to finalize rules in September requiring critical infrastructure operators to disclose cyberattacks. Industry groups have been lobbying CISA to align the new reporting deadlines and disclosure requirements with existing regulations.

title: US Cyber Agency Uses Anthropic's Mythos to Audit Government Code
summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency is using Anthropic's Mythos AI model to scan federal technology systems for vulnerabilities, according to people familiar with the matter. The arrangement comes even as Anthropic has been at odds with the White House for months over how its models can be used by the US government.

title: Facing a Revolt, HubSpot Reverses Its Decision to Use Customer Data For AI Feature
summary: HubSpot reversed a July 1 plan to collect and potentially share customers' CRM data by default to power a new AI sales-lead feature, after customers objected publicly and threatened to switch providers. HubSpot's chief product and technology officer called the terms-of-service changes "a mistake," in a reversal that echoes earlier customer-data backlashes faced by Slack and Zoom over AI training uses.

title: Beijing Considers Restricting Overseas Access to Top Chinese AI Models
summary: Chinese officials, led by the Ministry of Commerce, have discussed restricting overseas access to China's most advanced AI models, including both closed- and open-source systems, according to people familiar with the discussions. The talks also touched on possible limits on who can invest in domestic AI startups, amid a broader US-China rivalry that has seen Washington impose and partly ease export controls on Anthropic's most advanced models.

title: Mercor Hits Over $2 Billion in Gross Annualized Revenue
summary: AI-focused talent marketplace Mercor surpassed a $2 billion gross annualized revenue run rate in June, double its pace earlier this year, driven by rising demand from AI app developers and Fortune 500 customers building or fine-tuning their own AI models. The company pays out 60-70% of that revenue to contractors and is profitable on a free-cash-flow basis.

title: TeraWulf Shares Soar on $19 Billion Anthropic Data Center Deal
summary: Data-center developer TeraWulf signed a 20-year lease agreement to provide Anthropic a purpose-built AI campus in Hawesville, Kentucky, a deal expected to generate about $19 billion in contracted revenue. TeraWulf shares jumped as much as 19% intraday before closing up nearly 5%, and the company is also selling its stake in a separate joint venture.

title: Micron Continues Automotive Drive With Ford Deal
summary: Ford Motor Company and Micron Technology signed a long-term agreement for Micron to supply memory chips for next-generation vehicle production, a week after Micron announced a similar supply deal with General Motors.

title: Australia Social Media Age-Checks Fall Short
summary: A new study reportedly found that major social media platforms are failing to consistently apply age-verification methods under Australia's landmark ban on social media accounts for under-16s, exposing early enforcement gaps in the law.

title: The Anti-Meta Smart Glasses Just Became a Unicorn
summary: Shenzhen-based smart-glasses startup Even Realities raised $150 million in a pre-Series B round led by Meituan and Tencent, reaching a $1 billion valuation. Founded by former Apple engineers, the company sells camera-free glasses with a heads-up display starting around $599, betting that privacy-focused hardware can differentiate it from Meta's and Snap's camera-equipped AI glasses.

title: Alibaba Fights the U.S. Blacklist, and Wins Round One
summary: A federal judge temporarily blocked the Pentagon from enforcing a new rule barring it from contracting with firms whose lobbyists also represent companies on its list of alleged Chinese military companies, pending a ruling on Alibaba's constitutional challenge. Alibaba was added to the Pentagon's expanded 188-company list in June and sued on June 23 to be removed from it.

title: Big Tech Drastically Undercounts AI's Water Use
summary: Microsoft, Google, and Amazon report only the water consumed directly for on-site cooling at their data centers, omitting the far larger volume evaporated at the power plants that supply their electricity, according to a Wall Street Journal analysis. Indirect water use has historically run about 12 times direct consumption, and in water-stressed Phoenix, data centers could account for more than 20% of city water use by 2031, up from about 3% today.
